494	## Failure modes and recovery
495	
496	| What happened | What to do |
497	| --- | --- |
498	| Linear MCP unavailable or ticket not found | Continue without the Linear context. Note in Links: "Linear ticket: AI-NNN (MCP unavailable at draft time)" and let the user fill in. |
499	| Branch doesn't match a Linear pattern | Skip the Linear lookup. Rely on design artifacts and conversation. |
500	| No design artifact, no ticket, no clear Why from the conversation | Stop. Ask the user: "I can't establish a specific Why for this PR from the available context. Can you summarize the motivation in 1-2 sentences?" |
501	| `gh pr create` fails (auth, network, no remote) | Surface the error to the user. Don't retry without diagnosing. |
502	| User rejects the draft | Take their feedback and rewrite. Don't argue. |
503	| User wants to skip the confirmation step | Honor it — but require an explicit "skip confirmation" or "just create it" from them. Default is to confirm. |
504	
505	## Common pitfalls
506	
507	| Pitfall | Why it bites | Fix |
508	| --- | --- | --- |
509	| Drafting before pre-flight checks | PR opened against stale base, with uncommitted work left behind | Run the pre-flight batch first |
510	| Not checking for an existing PR | Duplicate PR, or `gh pr create` errors out | Always `gh pr view` first |
511	| Pasting the Linear ticket verbatim | Description becomes a wall of duplicated text | Paraphrase the problem statement; link the rest |
512	| Filling all sections regardless of signal | Skim-defeating filler | Drop sections that don't carry meaning |
513	| Autopiloting `gh pr create` | Premature publication; harder to retract than to delay | Show draft, wait for confirmation |
514	| Inheriting the default 🤖 footer | Violates the repo's no-AI-attribution rule | Strip it from the body |
515	| Trusting a clean roborev as proof the code runs | Roborev reviews the diff, not test execution — a hardcoded test assertion (e.g. a literal YAML `if:` string) can still fail in CI | Run the mirrored test file / grep for affected literals before roborev (Step 5) |
516	| Using "WIP" in title instead of `--draft` | Title noise; doesn't actually mark the PR as draft | Use `gh pr create --draft` and a clean title |
517	| Linking to the PR's own branch name as "context" | The branch is implicit; this is noise | Only link to artifacts that aren't already obvious from the PR |
518	| Forgetting the linked GitHub issue entirely | Issue lingers open after merge with no trace back to the PR that fixed it | Resolve it in Step 2, `Closes #NNN` in Step 7, record disposition in Step 9, comment in Step 12b |
519	| Drafting `Closes #NNN` in Step 7 but the final body sent to `gh pr create` drops it (edits, re-drafts, template drift) | Issue never auto-closes even though Step 2/9 correctly flagged full resolution — happened for real on gtm-sdk#609/#628 | Step 12's mechanical grep gate on the literal `--body` string, not on what Step 7 intended to write |
520	
521	## Red flags (stop and rethink)
522	
523	- **About to `git push` without running `roborev review --wait` first.** This is the repository-wide roborev gate defined in the repo's agent instructions; no PR should skip it.
524	- **About to `git push` with more commits than the PR needs.** Squash to a coherent set first (Step 4); don't rely on GitHub's "Squash and merge" button to clean up history before review.
525	- Drafting a PR with no Linear ticket, no design artifact, and no conversation-derived motivation.
526	- Writing more than 3 paragraphs in Why. If you need that much, the work is probably two PRs.
527	- Including a `## Summary` section. This is the default template's tell — replace with `## Why`.
528	- Including a 🤖 footer.
529	- More than 5 bullets in any one section. Each bullet should be load-bearing.
530	- A title that ends in a period, or starts with "Update", "Fix some", "Misc", "Various".
531	- A title that uses a Conventional Commits prefix (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`). PR titles are formal sentences, not commit subjects.
532	- A title that describes *what* the diff does (e.g., "Add X helper", "Refactor Y module") when a *why* framing was available.

546	# Creating Pull Requests
547	
548	## The principle: why over what
549	
550	A PR description's job is to give the reviewer what the diff *can't*: motivation, alternatives considered, risks worth scrutinizing, and a trail back to the originating context. The diff itself is the source of truth for what changed — paraphrasing it in the description is duplicate work that rots the moment someone force-pushes.
551	
552	Concretely:
553	
554	- Lead with the **problem**, not the change.
555	- Name the **alternatives** you considered, briefly. Skip if there were no meaningful ones.
556	- Call out what reviewers should **scrutinize**, not what they should take on faith.
557	- Link the **breadcrumb trail** — Linear ticket, design spec/plan, predecessor PR.
558	- **Never** summarize the diff. The reviewer is about to read it.
559	
560	A reader who skims your description should walk away with the mental model needed to read the diff with intention.
561	
562	## Workflow
563	
564	### Step 1: Pre-flight checks
565	
566	Before drafting, run these in a single batch of parallel `Bash` calls:
567	
568	```bash
569	git status                                          # working tree clean?
570	git branch --show-current                           # current branch?
571	git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream} 2>/dev/null  # is there a remote tracking ref?
572	git log @{upstream}..HEAD --oneline 2>/dev/null     # any unpushed commits?
573	git log main..HEAD --oneline                        # commits beyond main?
574	git diff main...HEAD --stat                         # surface area?
575	gh pr view --json url,state 2>/dev/null             # does a PR already exist?
576	gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name  # confirm base
577	```
578	
579	Stop and surface the problem to the user if any of these is true:
580	
581	- The working tree has uncommitted changes — ask the user whether to commit, stash, or abandon.
582	- The branch has no upstream / is not pushed — confirm with the user before pushing.
583	- The branch has zero commits beyond the base — there's nothing to PR.
584	- A PR already exists for this branch — use `gh pr edit` to update it, not `gh pr create`.
585	
586	Don't paper over these by force-pushing, amending, or running `git push -f`. The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) apply: destructive operations need explicit user approval.
587	
588	### Step 2: Gather context for the "Why"
589	
590	A strong Why section comes from upstream artifacts, not from the diff. Pull from these sources in parallel where possible:
591	
592	**Linear ticket** — if the branch name matches `(feature|agent)/<team>-<number>-<slug>` (e.g., `feature/ai-268-foo`, `agent/eng-1234-bar`):
593	
594	1. Extract the ticket ID with a regex like `[A-Z]+-\d+` (case-insensitive).
595	2. Read it via `mcp__linear__get_issue` with the identifier.
596	3. Lift the problem statement and acceptance criteria into the Why section — **paraphrase, don't paste**. A wall of quoted ticket text isn't a PR description.
597	4. Save the URL for the Links section.
598	
599	Skip the Linear lookup when the repo doesn't use Linear (no Linear MCP configured, no matching branch pattern) — rely on the sources below.
600	
601	**GitHub issue** — if the user linked or named a GitHub issue this session (a URL, `#NNN`, or an issue the branch was created for, e.g., `conductor/gtm-sdk-issue-608`):
602	
603	1. Note whether it's same-repo or cross-repo (a bare `#NNN` or number is same-repo; a URL or `owner/repo#NNN` names the repo explicitly — keep that `owner/repo` around for every later step). Fetch it with `gh issue view <number>` for a same-repo issue, or `gh issue view <number> --repo <owner/repo>` otherwise, to confirm it's still open and pull the problem statement into the Why section — paraphrase, don't paste.
604	2. Ask yourself (and, if unclear, the user) whether this PR **fully** resolves the issue or only partial work. Carry that determination into Step 7's Links section and Step 9.
605	3. Save the issue reference for the Links section either way.
606	
607	**Design artifacts** — scan `design/` (when the repo uses the design-artifact convention) for backlog/done files matching the branch topic:
608	
609	```bash
610	ls "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/design/" 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "<topic-keyword>"
611	```
612	
613	- `*-spec-*.md` files carry motivation, constraints, trade-offs.
614	- `*-plan-*.md` files carry scope (and by elision, what's out of scope).
615	- Read the matching artifact in full before drafting.
616	
617	**Git history**:
618	
619	- `git log main..HEAD --format='%s%n%b%n---'` — commit subjects and bodies often capture in-flight decisions better than the final diff.
620	
621	**Current conversation**:
622	
623	- If the user discussed alternatives, made decisions mid-flight, or set constraints earlier in this session, those belong in Trade-offs or Risks.
624	
625	If none of these sources establishes a clear Why, **stop and ask the user**. Don't fabricate motivation — a confident-sounding-but-vague Why is worse than asking.
626	
627	### Step 3: Commit local changes
628	
629	If the pre-flight check surfaced uncommitted changes that belong in this PR, commit them **before** running roborev — roborev reviews committed history, not the working tree, so uncommitted edits would be invisible to it.
630	
631	- Stage only the files that belong in this PR. Skip tool-local cruft (e.g., `.agents/`, `.claude/`, Conductor-local files) unless the user explicitly opts in.
632	- Commit without asking for approval: run `git commit` directly once the files are staged. The commit message should mirror the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) — not a Conventional Commits subject. The Step 8 draft approval is still the only user-approval gate before push.
633	- Do **not** push yet. Push happens in Step 11, after squash, roborev, the user-confirmation gate, and the rebase.
634	
635	If the working tree is already clean, skip this step.
636	
637	### Step 4: Squash to a coherent set of commits
638	
639	**Hard gate: squash before roborev, roborev before the user-confirmation gate, confirmation before push.** All three must happen before the branch hits `origin` so the review (and the merge) operate on the final history, not a noisy timeline.
640	
641	```bash
642	git log main..HEAD --oneline
643	```
644	
645	- **Default to one commit per PR.** Multi-commit PRs are only OK when each commit is independently reviewable and the slices land in order.
646	- Squash with `git rebase -i main` or `git reset --soft main && git commit`. Never use `--no-edit` flags that bypass message review.
647	- The squashed commit message mirrors the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) and captures the motivation in the body. No Conventional Commits prefix.
648	- If the branch already has a single commit (or each existing commit is independently reviewable and ordered), skip the rebase but still confirm the count before moving on.
649	- **Never force-push to a shared branch to squash after publication.** Squash *before* the first push.
650	
651	### Step 5: Run relevant tests locally, then roborev review before drafting
652	
653	**Roborev reviews the diff; it does not execute the test suite.** A clean roborev pass says nothing about whether the code runs — it has caught logic/quality issues while a hardcoded assertion in a test file was still broken. Before roborev, run whatever tests cover the changed files:
654	
655	- Identify affected tests by mirroring the changed path under `tests/` (many repos mirror source layout — a change to `pkg/foo.py` often has a matching `tests/.../test_foo.py`) and/or `grep -rn` the changed file's distinctive strings (a literal like an `if:` condition, a flag name) across `tests/` to catch assertions on exact values.
656	- Run the narrowest test target that covers the change (in a uv-based Python repo, `uv run pytest tests/<mirrored-path>`; otherwise the repo's own test command) — full-suite runs are fine too, but don't skip this step because CI will "catch it anyway": local runs take seconds, CI takes minutes.
657	- If a test fails, fix it now and fold the fix into the same commit (Step 3/4), *before* running roborev — don't push and let CI discover it.
658	
659	**Hard gate: do not draft the PR or move toward `git push` until roborev has run and either reported clean or been explicitly acknowledged by the user.** This applies even if the change feels trivial, even if the diff is one line, and even if the user has not asked for review explicitly — the skill always runs roborev before the user is asked to approve a draft.
660	
661	With the squashed commit in place but the branch still local, run a local AI code review with roborev so findings surface *before* the user sees a draft and *before* GitHub sees the diff. Invoke the `roborev` executable directly with the `--wait` flag; Git aliases are optional conveniences and may not exist in cloud sandboxes:
662	
663	```bash
664	roborev review --wait
665	```
666	
667	- `--wait` is **required**, not optional — it blocks until the review completes so findings are available before the draft is shown. Do not run `roborev review` without `--wait`.
668	- A bare `roborev review` — or a leftover post-commit auto-review hook — only **enqueues a background daemon job and returns before a verdict exists**. An enqueue is not a pass: if HEAD already has a queued or running background review, block on it (`roborev review --wait`, or `roborev wait` for the already-enqueued job) so an actual verdict is in hand before drafting. Never report "review enqueued" or a missing verdict as clean.
669	- Capture the outcome (clean, N findings fixed in M rounds, N findings unresolved, unavailable) — Step 8 surfaces it inside the draft preview so the user can see the gate was walked.
670	- **Review loop (no permission prompts):** if roborev surfaces findings, fix them yourself without asking — **every severity counts**, including low and nit. Do not stop, summarize, or ask "fix these?" / "defer or proceed?" because findings are low severity. Fix as many as possible that are small in scope: a wording or error-message change, a missing test case, a missing guard, a rename, a local refactor inside the changed function. Do not fix findings that would reshape the surrounding design, change public interfaces, or touch files outside this PR's scope; for those only, report them to the user with the reason they were not fixed. Put the fixes in a follow-up commit, re-squash (Step 4), and re-run `roborev review --wait` (this step). Repeat until a run comes back clean or only out-of-scope findings remain. Do not ask "fix and rerun?" — that is the default action.
671	- **Loop cap:** stop after 3 fix rounds. If findings remain, or a finding would need a product or design decision rather than a code fix, stop looping and list the unresolved findings in the Step 8 draft preview, so the user decides at the single approval gate. Never amend or force-push past findings silently.
672	- If roborev is unavailable (command not installed, no network), say so explicitly to the user and ask whether to proceed without review. Do not silently skip.
673	- For deeper fix/refine loops, consult the repo's roborev guide skill if it ships one.
674	
675	### Step 6: Draft the title
676	
677	The title is a formal, sentence-cased statement of **why this change exists** — not a conventional commit subject. A reviewer scanning the PR list should understand the *motivation*, not just the area of code touched.
678	
679	Rules:
680	
681	- **Formal, sentence case.** "Eliminate duplicated Attio retry logic across five call sites" — not "attio retry refactor".
682	- **Lead with the why, not the what.** Prefer the problem solved or the outcome enabled over the mechanical change. "Unblock Linear → Attio sync from rate-limit drift" beats "Add retry decorator to Attio client".
683	- **No Conventional Commits prefix.** Do **not** use `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, etc. Even if recent commits or PRs use them, PR titles in this ecosystem are full sentences. Commit messages and PR titles are different surfaces.
684	- **Under 70 characters where possible**, but clarity wins over brevity — GitHub truncates in list views, so front-load the most important words.
685	- **Specific.** "Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts" — not "Bug fix" or "Improvements".
686	- **No ticket IDs in the title.** They go in Links.
687	- **No trailing period.**
688	- **Avoid bare imperative verbs** like "Add", "Fix", "Update" as the first word when a why-framing is possible. They're allowed when the why genuinely is the action (e.g., a clear bugfix), but check first whether the motivation can lead instead.
689	
690	Good vs. bad title shapes:
691	
692	| Bad (conventional / what-focused) | Good (formal / why-focused) |
693	| --- | --- |
694	| `feat: add retry decorator` | `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear sync` |
695	| `fix: pagination bug` | `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts` |
696	| `refactor: clean up attio client` | `Eliminate divergent retry behavior across Attio call sites` |
697	| `chore: bump deps` | `Bump httpx to 0.27 to pick up the connection-pool leak fix` |
698	
699	### Step 7: Draft the description
700	
701	Use this template. **Drop sections that have nothing meaningful in them** — a section containing "None" or "N/A" is worse than no section.
702	
703	```markdown
704	## Why
705	<1-3 paragraphs. Lead with the problem or constraint. State the motivation. Reference upstream context (ticket, spec) by link, not paraphrase. The reviewer should finish this section understanding what would happen if the PR were *not* merged.>
706	
707	## Trade-offs
708	<Only if there were meaningful alternatives. Format: "Chose X over Y because Z." Skip if the approach was obvious or there was only one reasonable way.>
709	
710	## Risks
711	<What could break that isn't already covered by tests. Note rollback path if non-trivial. Skip for clearly low-risk changes (docs, comments, isolated refactors with full coverage).>
712	
713	## Test plan
714	<Reasoning, not output. "Exercised X path with Y inputs because Z is the highest-risk surface." If full unit coverage exists and the change is small/obvious, skip this section.>
715	
716	## Links
717	- Linear: [TEAM-NNN](https://linear.app/...)
718	- Spec: design/backlog-...-spec-01.md
719	- Plan: design/backlog-...-plan-01.md
720	- Related PRs: #NNN
721	- Closes #NNN (only when Step 2 confirmed this PR fully resolves a same-repo GitHub issue)
722	```
723	
724	Section guidance:
725	
726	| Section | Required? | When to drop it |
727	| --- | --- | --- |
728	| Why | Always | Never. If you can't write a specific one, the work isn't ready. |
729	| Trade-offs | When meaningful alternatives existed | Obvious one-way changes, fixes to clear bugs |
730	| Risks | When the change has non-trivial blast radius | Docs, comments, isolated refactors with coverage |
731	| Test plan | When testing required judgment calls | Small changes with full unit coverage |
732	| Links | If any upstream artifact exists | True greenfield work with no ticket, spec, or predecessor PR |
733	
734	### Step 8: Show the draft. Wait for confirmation. (Single approval gate before push.)
735	
736	**This is the only user-approval gate in the workflow, and it sits immediately before `git push`.** Steps 3–5 (commit, squash, roborev) must already be complete by the time you reach it — by construction the agent cannot honor a "yes" without having walked the roborev gate first.
737	
738	Show the draft title, the draft body, **and the roborev outcome** so the user can see the gate was walked. Even if the user said "create a PR", they agreed to the action, not blind-trusted your draft.
739	
740	**Shortcut:** If the user re-sends this *exact* create_pr prompt verbatim, or an explicit approval phrase like "create/open the PR now," immediately after the agent has already shown a draft under this step, treat that as the Step 8 approval — proceed exactly as a "yes" would (Steps 9–13), don't re-run Steps 1–7 to produce a fresh draft. Anything else — a revision request, a question about the draft, or a paraphrase — is not the shortcut; treat it as normal feedback and re-show the draft.
741	
742	Format the preview as:
743	
744	```text
745	Title: <draft title>
746	
747	Body:
748	---
749	<draft body>
750	---
751	
752	Roborev: <clean (after M fix rounds) | N findings unresolved (list them) | unavailable (reason)>
753	
754	Push and create this PR? (or edit before I submit)
755	```
756	
757	The roborev line is mandatory — never omit it. If it shows "unavailable", the user is implicitly being asked to proceed without review.
758	
759	If the user requests edits, revise and re-show. Don't auto-submit. A "yes" here authorizes closing or linking the GitHub issue (Step 9), the rebase (Step 10), the push (Step 11), and the PR creation (Step 12) — proceed through all of them without re-prompting (pausing only if the rebase hits conflicts).
760	
761	### Step 9: Note the GitHub issue disposition
762	
763	If Step 2 identified a GitHub issue this PR addresses, carry its disposition forward — the actual action happens in Step 12b, once a PR URL exists:
764	
765	- **Same-repo issue, fully resolved by this PR** — the `Closes #NNN` line already lives in the PR body (Step 7's Links section). Nothing further is needed here: GitHub auto-closes the issue when the PR merges into `main`. Don't `gh issue close` it now — the fix isn't on `main` yet.
766	- **Cross-repo issue, or only partially resolved** — GitHub's closing keywords don't work across repos and shouldn't be used for partial work. Remember to leave a linking comment in Step 12b instead of closing it.
767	- **Ambiguous whether this PR fully resolves it** — this should already have been resolved in Step 2; if it wasn't, ask the user now rather than guessing at merge-closing behavior.
768	- Skip silently if no GitHub issue was identified in Step 2.
769	- Already authorized by the Step 8 "yes" — don't re-prompt.
770	
771	### Step 10: Rebase onto the latest base (last step before opening the PR)
772	
773	**This is the final step before the PR is opened.** Immediately before pushing, rebase the branch onto the freshest base so the PR opens against current `main` and merge conflicts surface here — locally, where they're cheap to resolve — instead of in GitHub's merge UI.
774	
775	This must happen **before** the first push (Step 11), not after. Rebasing a branch that's already on `origin` would require a force-push, which is forbidden without explicit user approval.
776	
777	```bash
778	git fetch origin
779	git rebase origin/main   # or the confirmed base branch from pre-flight
780	```
781	
782	- If the rebase is clean, proceed to Step 11.
783	- If the rebase hits conflicts, **stop and surface them to the user.** Resolve them (or have the user resolve them), then re-run Steps 4–5 (re-squash if needed, re-run `roborev review --wait`) so the review reflects the rebased history. Never `git rebase --skip` or abandon conflicting hunks silently.
784	- If the branch is already up to date with the base, the rebase is a no-op — proceed.
785	
786	### Step 11: Push the branch
787	
788	Once the rebase is clean, push the branch to `origin` with upstream tracking.
789	
790	```bash
791	git push -u origin "$(git branch --show-current)"
792	```
793	
794	Confirm the push succeeded before moving on. If it fails (auth, protected branch, non-fast-forward), surface the error and stop — do not force-push.
795	
796	### Step 12: Create the PR
797	
798	**Hard gate before running `gh pr create`: for every same-repo GitHub issue Step 2 determined this PR fully resolves, mechanically verify the drafted body contains a `Closes #NNN` / `Fixes #NNN` / `Resolves #NNN` line for *that specific* issue number before shelling out — one PR can fully resolve more than one issue, and each needs its own closing reference, not just the first.** This is a real known failure mode, not a hypothetical: gtm-sdk#609 was fully fixed by gtm-sdk#628, but the drafted body only listed "gtm-sdk#609" under Links without a closing keyword, so GitHub never auto-closed it and it sat open until manually closed later. A "the plan said to add it" belief is not sufficient — grep the actual string you're about to pass to `--body` for the pattern before running the command, once per fully-resolved issue number:
799	
800	```bash
801	grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY"
802	```
803	
804	`\b` is not portable to the BSD `grep` on macOS — use the `([^[:alnum:]_]|$)` form above instead, which matches the same "word boundary or end of string" intent on both BSD and GNU grep.
805	
806	If that grep fails for any fully-resolved issue number, **stop and fix the body** — don't proceed to `gh pr create` with a body that silently downgraded to a bare reference. If Step 2 flagged partial/cross-repo instead, the grep is expected to fail and that's correct — don't add the keyword in that case.
807	
808	To make this checkable, assign the HEREDOC to `PR_BODY` first, grep that exact variable, then pass it to `--body` — don't construct the body inline in the `gh pr create` call, since there's nothing to grep before shelling out:
809	
810	```bash
811	PR_BODY="$(cat <<'EOF'
812	## Why
813	... (real newlines, not \n)
814	EOF
815	)"
816	
817	for ISSUE_NUMBER in "${FULLY_RESOLVED_ISSUE_NUMBERS[@]}"; do  # every issue Step 2 flagged as fully resolved
818	  grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY" || {
819	    echo "missing closing keyword for #${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >&2
820	    exit 1
821	  }
822	done
823	
824	gh pr create --title "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup that double-charged credits" --body "$PR_BODY"
825	```
826	
827	Return the PR URL to the user. Don't add follow-up commentary unless the user asks — the URL is the work product.
828	
829	### Step 12b: Link the GitHub issue, if Step 9 deferred it
830	
831	Only applies when Step 9 flagged a **cross-repo or partially-resolved** issue — the fully-resolved same-repo case already carries its `Closes #NNN` in the PR body and needs no action here.
832	
833	```bash
834	gh issue comment <number> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>"                    # same-repo, partial
835	gh issue comment <number> --repo <owner/repo> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>" # cross-repo — use the owner/repo saved in Step 2
836	```
837	
838	- `<PR URL>` is the output from Step 12 — this step cannot run before Step 12 for exactly that reason.
839	- Do not close the issue yourself; partial or cross-repo work isn't the maintainer's signal to close it.
840	- Skip silently if Step 9 found nothing to do here.
841	
842	### Step 13: Suggest the merge once tests and checks pass
843	
844	Merging is never automatic. Once the PR is open, check its status with a single call (`gh pr checks <pr-number>`). When tests and required checks have passed, suggest merging with the GitHub CLI and wait for the user to say yes:
845	
846	```bash
847	gh pr merge <pr-number> --squash
848	```
849	
850	- Do not poll in a loop. If checks are still running, report that and stop; the user can ask again later.
851	- Do not log in to, configure, or call any merge-queue service. If `gh` is not authenticated, say so and stop.
852	- Never pass `--admin` or `--auto` unless the user asks for it.
853	
854	## Modifiers: drafts, reviewers, labels
855	
856	`gh pr create` accepts modifiers that don't affect the description but matter for the PR's lifecycle. Don't auto-set any of these; only pass what the user explicitly asks for:
857	
858	| Flag | When |
859	| --- | --- |
860	| `--draft` | User says "draft", or commit history shows clear in-progress markers ("WIP", "spike"). |
861	| `--reviewer <handle>` | Only when the user names reviewers. Don't guess. |
862	| `--label <name>` | Only labels that exist (`gh label list`). Invented labels silently no-op. |
863	| `--assignee <handle>` | Default to `@me` unless told otherwise. |
864	| `--base <branch>` | Only override the default branch when the user says so. |
865	
866	## Anti-patterns
867	
868	These show up in autogenerated PR descriptions and this skill must actively avoid them. Several come from defaults baked into other tools — including the default `gh pr create` template suggested by the Bash tool — and this skill overrides them.
869	
870	### Don't summarize the diff
871	
872	```markdown
873	## Summary
874	- Added `retry_with_backoff` helper in `apollo/client.py`
875	- Updated `enrich_account` to use it
876	- Added 3 unit tests in `test_apollo.py`
877	```
878	
879	The reviewer is about to read the diff. This is duplicate work that rots the moment the diff changes. Replace with **Why**.
880	
881	### Don't write empty sections
882	
883	```markdown
884	## Risks
885	None.
886	
887	## Test plan
888	Tested locally.
889	```
890	
891	"None" and "Tested locally" carry zero signal. Drop the section.
892	
893	### Don't add AI attribution
894	
895	The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) prohibit AI attribution in commits and PRs.
896	**Never** emit:
897	
898	- `Co-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>`
899	- `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](...)`
900	- Any "Generated by ..." or "Powered by ..." footer
901	
902	The Bash tool's default PR template includes the 🤖 footer. **Strip it.** This skill overrides that default.
903	
904	### Don't restate the title
905	
906	If the title is "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup", the description shouldn't open with "This PR fixes a race in the Apollo enrichment dedup logic." Start the Why with the problem, not a rephrase.
907	
908	### Don't pad with boilerplate
909	
910	- "This PR makes some improvements to ..."
911	- "As discussed offline, ..."
912	- "Cleaning up some technical debt ..."
913	
914	If you can't write a specific Why, pause and ask the user. Vague motivation is a tell that the work isn't ready for review.
915	
916	### Don't paste test output
917	
918	The Test plan section is about the *reasoning* behind what was tested. A reviewer can run the tests. They cannot rederive your reasoning from the output.
919	
920	### Don't include "Closes #NNN" without confirming
921	
922	GitHub auto-closes referenced issues on merge. Only use `Closes` / `Fixes` / `Resolves` keywords if Step 2 confirmed the PR fully resolves a **same-repo** issue. For partial work or a cross-repo issue, mention it in Links instead and leave a linking comment on the issue in Step 12b — no magic keyword. Skipping the confirmation in Step 2 is a bug, not a safe default: it leaves the issue open with no trace back to the PR that addressed it.
923	
924	### Don't autopilot the PR submission
925	
926	Even if the user said "create a PR for this", they agreed to the action, not to a specific draft. Show the draft, wait for confirmation, then submit.
927	
928	## Examples
929	
930	### Example 1: Small bug fix — Why + Links only
931	
932	**Title:** `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts`
933	
934	**Body:**
935	
936	```markdown
937	## Why
938	The Apollo `search_people` paginator was dropping the last page of results because the cursor check used `>` instead of `>=`. Affected every batch where total results were an exact multiple of page_size — roughly 10% of runs. Caught when a TAM build was missing ~50 known contacts ([AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)).
939	
940	## Links
941	- Linear: [AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)
942	```
943	
944	(Trade-offs, Risks, Test plan dropped — small obvious fix, full coverage exists.)
945	
946	### Example 2: Refactor — Why + Trade-offs + Risks + Links
947	
948	**Title:** `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear → Attio sync`
949	
950	**Body:**
951	
952	```markdown
953	## Why
954	Five call sites in `libs/attio/` were duplicating retry/backoff logic, and each had drifted: `update_person` retried on 5xx but not 429; `create_person` retried on 429 but with no backoff; `list_workspaces` did no retry at all. The new Linear → Attio sync was about to become the sixth divergent copy.
955	
956	Pulling the logic into `@retry_with_backoff` lets callers opt in with one line and ensures consistent behavior across all Attio writes.
957	
958	## Trade-offs
959	Considered `tenacity` instead. Rejected because the call sites already have idiosyncratic logic — custom backoff that respects Attio's `Retry-After` header — that `tenacity` would require a custom wait strategy to express. The hand-rolled decorator is ~30 lines and stays close to the Attio-specific behavior.
960	
961	## Risks
962	Changes the *shape* of exceptions that bubble up: `AttioRateLimit` is now wrapped in `RetryExhausted` after N attempts. Two existing callers caught `AttioRateLimit` directly; both updated in this PR. Grep for `AttioRateLimit` returns no other matches.
963	
964	## Links
965	- Linear: [AI-2891](https://linear.app/...)
966	- Spec: design/backlog-202604010000-attio_retry_decorator-spec-01.md
967	```
968	
969	### Example 3: Bad → Good
970	
971	**Bad:**
972	
973	```markdown
974	## Summary
975	- Added retry decorator
976	- Updated 5 Attio call sites
977	- Removed duplicate retry code
978	- Added tests
979	
980	## Test plan
981	- [x] Ran tests
982	- [x] Tested locally
983	
984	🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
985	```
986	
987	What's wrong: the Summary paraphrases the diff, the Test plan has no reasoning, the AI footer is forbidden, and there's no motivation a reviewer can use to evaluate the change.
988	
989	**Good:** see Example 2.
990	
991	## Failure modes and recovery
992	
993	| What happened | What to do |
994	| --- | --- |
995	| Linear MCP unavailable or ticket not found | Continue without the Linear context. Note in Links: "Linear ticket: AI-NNN (MCP unavailable at draft time)" and let the user fill in. |
996	| Branch doesn't match a Linear pattern | Skip the Linear lookup. Rely on design artifacts and conversation. |
997	| No design artifact, no ticket, no clear Why from the conversation | Stop. Ask the user: "I can't establish a specific Why for this PR from the available context. Can you summarize the motivation in 1-2 sentences?" |
998	| `gh pr create` fails (auth, network, no remote) | Surface the error to the user. Don't retry without diagnosing. |
999	| User rejects the draft | Take their feedback and rewrite. Don't argue. |
1000	| User wants to skip the confirmation step | Honor it — but require an explicit "skip confirmation" or "just create it" from them. Default is to confirm. |
1001	
1002	## Common pitfalls
1003	
1004	| Pitfall | Why it bites | Fix |
1005	| --- | --- | --- |
1006	| Drafting before pre-flight checks | PR opened against stale base, with uncommitted work left behind | Run the pre-flight batch first |
1007	| Not checking for an existing PR | Duplicate PR, or `gh pr create` errors out | Always `gh pr view` first |
1008	| Pasting the Linear ticket verbatim | Description becomes a wall of duplicated text | Paraphrase the problem statement; link the rest |
1009	| Filling all sections regardless of signal | Skim-defeating filler | Drop sections that don't carry meaning |
1010	| Autopiloting `gh pr create` | Premature publication; harder to retract than to delay | Show draft, wait for confirmation |
1011	| Inheriting the default 🤖 footer | Violates the repo's no-AI-attribution rule | Strip it from the body |
1012	| Trusting a clean roborev as proof the code runs | Roborev reviews the diff, not test execution — a hardcoded test assertion (e.g. a literal YAML `if:` string) can still fail in CI | Run the mirrored test file / grep for affected literals before roborev (Step 5) |
1013	| Using "WIP" in title instead of `--draft` | Title noise; doesn't actually mark the PR as draft | Use `gh pr create --draft` and a clean title |
1014	| Linking to the PR's own branch name as "context" | The branch is implicit; this is noise | Only link to artifacts that aren't already obvious from the PR |
1015	| Forgetting the linked GitHub issue entirely | Issue lingers open after merge with no trace back to the PR that fixed it | Resolve it in Step 2, `Closes #NNN` in Step 7, record disposition in Step 9, comment in Step 12b |
1016	| Drafting `Closes #NNN` in Step 7 but the final body sent to `gh pr create` drops it (edits, re-drafts, template drift) | Issue never auto-closes even though Step 2/9 correctly flagged full resolution — happened for real on gtm-sdk#609/#628 | Step 12's mechanical grep gate on the literal `--body` string, not on what Step 7 intended to write |
1017	
1018	## Red flags (stop and rethink)
1019	
1020	- **About to `git push` without running `roborev review --wait` first.** This is the repository-wide roborev gate defined in the repo's agent instructions; no PR should skip it.
1021	- **About to `git push` with more commits than the PR needs.** Squash to a coherent set first (Step 4); don't rely on GitHub's "Squash and merge" button to clean up history before review.
1022	- Drafting a PR with no Linear ticket, no design artifact, and no conversation-derived motivation.
1023	- Writing more than 3 paragraphs in Why. If you need that much, the work is probably two PRs.
1024	- Including a `## Summary` section. This is the default template's tell — replace with `## Why`.
1025	- Including a 🤖 footer.
1026	- More than 5 bullets in any one section. Each bullet should be load-bearing.
1027	- A title that ends in a period, or starts with "Update", "Fix some", "Misc", "Various".
1028	- A title that uses a Conventional Commits prefix (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`). PR titles are formal sentences, not commit subjects.
1029	- A title that describes *what* the diff does (e.g., "Add X helper", "Refactor Y module") when a *why* framing was available.

     scripts/install-conductor-prompts.py — do not hand-edit the TOML copy.

# Creating Pull Requests

## The principle: why over what

A PR description's job is to give the reviewer what the diff *can't*: motivation, alternatives considered, risks worth scrutinizing, and a trail back to the originating context. The diff itself is the source of truth for what changed — paraphrasing it in the description is duplicate work that rots the moment someone force-pushes.

Concretely:

- Lead with the **problem**, not the change.
- Name the **alternatives** you considered, briefly. Skip if there were no meaningful ones.
- Call out what reviewers should **scrutinize**, not what they should take on faith.
- Link the **breadcrumb trail** — Linear ticket, design spec/plan, predecessor PR.
- **Never** summarize the diff. The reviewer is about to read it.

A reader who skims your description should walk away with the mental model needed to read the diff with intention.

## Workflow

### Step 1: Pre-flight checks

Before drafting, run these in a single batch of parallel `Bash` calls:

```bash
git status                                          # working tree clean?
git branch --show-current                           # current branch?
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream} 2>/dev/null  # is there a remote tracking ref?
git log @{upstream}..HEAD --oneline 2>/dev/null     # any unpushed commits?
git log main..HEAD --oneline                        # commits beyond main?
git diff main...HEAD --stat                         # surface area?
gh pr view --json url,state 2>/dev/null             # does a PR already exist?
gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name  # confirm base
```

Stop and surface the problem to the user if any of these is true:

- The working tree has uncommitted changes — ask the user whether to commit, stash, or abandon.
- The branch has no upstream / is not pushed — confirm with the user before pushing.
- The branch has zero commits beyond the base — there's nothing to PR.
- A PR already exists for this branch — use `gh pr edit` to update it, not `gh pr create`.

Don't paper over these by force-pushing, amending, or running `git push -f`. The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) apply: destructive operations need explicit user approval.

### Step 2: Gather context for the "Why"

A strong Why section comes from upstream artifacts, not from the diff. Pull from these sources in parallel where possible:

**Linear ticket** — if the branch name matches `(feature|agent)/<team>-<number>-<slug>` (e.g., `feature/ai-268-foo`, `agent/eng-1234-bar`):

1. Extract the ticket ID with a regex like `[A-Z]+-\d+` (case-insensitive).
2. Read it via `mcp__linear__get_issue` with the identifier.
3. Lift the problem statement and acceptance criteria into the Why section — **paraphrase, don't paste**. A wall of quoted ticket text isn't a PR description.
4. Save the URL for the Links section.

Skip the Linear lookup when the repo doesn't use Linear (no Linear MCP configured, no matching branch pattern) — rely on the sources below.

**GitHub issue** — if the user linked or named a GitHub issue this session (a URL, `#NNN`, or an issue the branch was created for, e.g., `conductor/gtm-sdk-issue-608`):

1. Note whether it's same-repo or cross-repo (a bare `#NNN` or number is same-repo; a URL or `owner/repo#NNN` names the repo explicitly — keep that `owner/repo` around for every later step). Fetch it with `gh issue view <number>` for a same-repo issue, or `gh issue view <number> --repo <owner/repo>` otherwise, to confirm it's still open and pull the problem statement into the Why section — paraphrase, don't paste.
2. Ask yourself (and, if unclear, the user) whether this PR **fully** resolves the issue or only partial work. Carry that determination into Step 7's Links section and Step 9.
3. Save the issue reference for the Links section either way.

**Design artifacts** — scan `design/` (when the repo uses the design-artifact convention) for backlog/done files matching the branch topic:

```bash
ls "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/design/" 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "<topic-keyword>"
```

- `*-spec-*.md` files carry motivation, constraints, trade-offs.
- `*-plan-*.md` files carry scope (and by elision, what's out of scope).
- Read the matching artifact in full before drafting.

**Git history**:

- `git log main..HEAD --format='%s%n%b%n---'` — commit subjects and bodies often capture in-flight decisions better than the final diff.

**Current conversation**:

- If the user discussed alternatives, made decisions mid-flight, or set constraints earlier in this session, those belong in Trade-offs or Risks.

If none of these sources establishes a clear Why, **stop and ask the user**. Don't fabricate motivation — a confident-sounding-but-vague Why is worse than asking.

### Step 3: Commit local changes

If the pre-flight check surfaced uncommitted changes that belong in this PR, commit them **before** running roborev — roborev reviews committed history, not the working tree, so uncommitted edits would be invisible to it.

- Stage only the files that belong in this PR. Skip tool-local cruft (e.g., `.agents/`, `.claude/`, Conductor-local files) unless the user explicitly opts in.
- Commit without asking for approval: run `git commit` directly once the files are staged. The commit message should mirror the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) — not a Conventional Commits subject. The Step 8 draft approval is still the only user-approval gate before push.
- Do **not** push yet. Push happens in Step 11, after squash, roborev, the user-confirmation gate, and the rebase.

If the working tree is already clean, skip this step.

### Step 4: Squash to a coherent set of commits

**Hard gate: squash before roborev, roborev before the user-confirmation gate, confirmation before push.** All three must happen before the branch hits `origin` so the review (and the merge) operate on the final history, not a noisy timeline.

```bash
git log main..HEAD --oneline
```

- **Default to one commit per PR.** Multi-commit PRs are only OK when each commit is independently reviewable and the slices land in order.
- Squash with `git rebase -i main` or `git reset --soft main && git commit`. Never use `--no-edit` flags that bypass message review.
- The squashed commit message mirrors the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) and captures the motivation in the body. No Conventional Commits prefix.
- If the branch already has a single commit (or each existing commit is independently reviewable and ordered), skip the rebase but still confirm the count before moving on.
- **Never force-push to a shared branch to squash after publication.** Squash *before* the first push.

### Step 5: Run relevant tests locally, then roborev review before drafting

**Roborev reviews the diff; it does not execute the test suite.** A clean roborev pass says nothing about whether the code runs — it has caught logic/quality issues while a hardcoded assertion in a test file was still broken. Before roborev, run whatever tests cover the changed files:

- Identify affected tests by mirroring the changed path under `tests/` (many repos mirror source layout — a change to `pkg/foo.py` often has a matching `tests/.../test_foo.py`) and/or `grep -rn` the changed file's distinctive strings (a literal like an `if:` condition, a flag name) across `tests/` to catch assertions on exact values.
- Run the narrowest test target that covers the change (in a uv-based Python repo, `uv run pytest tests/<mirrored-path>`; otherwise the repo's own test command) — full-suite runs are fine too, but don't skip this step because CI will "catch it anyway": local runs take seconds, CI takes minutes.
- If a test fails, fix it now and fold the fix into the same commit (Step 3/4), *before* running roborev — don't push and let CI discover it.

**Hard gate: do not draft the PR or move toward `git push` until roborev has run and either reported clean or been explicitly acknowledged by the user.** This applies even if the change feels trivial, even if the diff is one line, and even if the user has not asked for review explicitly — the skill always runs roborev before the user is asked to approve a draft.

With the squashed commit in place but the branch still local, run a local AI code review with roborev so findings surface *before* the user sees a draft and *before* GitHub sees the diff. Invoke the `roborev` executable directly with the `--wait` flag; Git aliases are optional conveniences and may not exist in cloud sandboxes:

```bash
roborev review --wait
```

- `--wait` is **required**, not optional — it blocks until the review completes so findings are available before the draft is shown. Do not run `roborev review` without `--wait`.
- A bare `roborev review` — or a leftover post-commit auto-review hook — only **enqueues a background daemon job and returns before a verdict exists**. An enqueue is not a pass: if HEAD already has a queued or running background review, block on it (`roborev review --wait`, or `roborev wait` for the already-enqueued job) so an actual verdict is in hand before drafting. Never report "review enqueued" or a missing verdict as clean.
- Capture the outcome (clean, N findings fixed in M rounds, N findings unresolved, unavailable) — Step 8 surfaces it inside the draft preview so the user can see the gate was walked.
- **Review loop (no permission prompts):** if roborev surfaces findings, fix them yourself without asking — **every severity counts**, including low and nit. Do not stop, summarize, or ask "fix these?" / "defer or proceed?" because findings are low severity. Fix as many as possible that are small in scope: a wording or error-message change, a missing test case, a missing guard, a rename, a local refactor inside the changed function. Do not fix findings that would reshape the surrounding design, change public interfaces, or touch files outside this PR's scope; for those only, report them to the user with the reason they were not fixed. Put the fixes in a follow-up commit, re-squash (Step 4), and re-run `roborev review --wait` (this step). Repeat until a run comes back clean or only out-of-scope findings remain. Do not ask "fix and rerun?" — that is the default action.
- **Loop cap:** stop after 3 fix rounds. If findings remain, or a finding would need a product or design decision rather than a code fix, stop looping and list the unresolved findings in the Step 8 draft preview, so the user decides at the single approval gate. Never amend or force-push past findings silently.
- If roborev is unavailable (command not installed, no network), say so explicitly to the user and ask whether to proceed without review. Do not silently skip.
- For deeper fix/refine loops, consult the repo's roborev guide skill if it ships one.

### Step 6: Draft the title

The title is a formal, sentence-cased statement of **why this change exists** — not a conventional commit subject. A reviewer scanning the PR list should understand the *motivation*, not just the area of code touched.

Rules:

- **Formal, sentence case.** "Eliminate duplicated Attio retry logic across five call sites" — not "attio retry refactor".
- **Lead with the why, not the what.** Prefer the problem solved or the outcome enabled over the mechanical change. "Unblock Linear → Attio sync from rate-limit drift" beats "Add retry decorator to Attio client".
- **No Conventional Commits prefix.** Do **not** use `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, etc. Even if recent commits or PRs use them, PR titles in this ecosystem are full sentences. Commit messages and PR titles are different surfaces.
- **Under 70 characters where possible**, but clarity wins over brevity — GitHub truncates in list views, so front-load the most important words.
- **Specific.** "Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts" — not "Bug fix" or "Improvements".
- **No ticket IDs in the title.** They go in Links.
- **No trailing period.**
- **Avoid bare imperative verbs** like "Add", "Fix", "Update" as the first word when a why-framing is possible. They're allowed when the why genuinely is the action (e.g., a clear bugfix), but check first whether the motivation can lead instead.

Good vs. bad title shapes:

| Bad (conventional / what-focused) | Good (formal / why-focused) |
| --- | --- |
| `feat: add retry decorator` | `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear sync` |
| `fix: pagination bug` | `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts` |
| `refactor: clean up attio client` | `Eliminate divergent retry behavior across Attio call sites` |
| `chore: bump deps` | `Bump httpx to 0.27 to pick up the connection-pool leak fix` |

### Step 7: Draft the description

Use this template. **Drop sections that have nothing meaningful in them** — a section containing "None" or "N/A" is worse than no section.

```markdown
## Why
<1-3 paragraphs. Lead with the problem or constraint. State the motivation. Reference upstream context (ticket, spec) by link, not paraphrase. The reviewer should finish this section understanding what would happen if the PR were *not* merged.>

## Trade-offs
<Only if there were meaningful alternatives. Format: "Chose X over Y because Z." Skip if the approach was obvious or there was only one reasonable way.>

## Risks
<What could break that isn't already covered by tests. Note rollback path if non-trivial. Skip for clearly low-risk changes (docs, comments, isolated refactors with full coverage).>

## Test plan
<Reasoning, not output. "Exercised X path with Y inputs because Z is the highest-risk surface." If full unit coverage exists and the change is small/obvious, skip this section.>

## Links
- Linear: [TEAM-NNN](https://linear.app/...)
- Spec: design/backlog-...-spec-01.md
- Plan: design/backlog-...-plan-01.md
- Related PRs: #NNN
- Closes #NNN (only when Step 2 confirmed this PR fully resolves a same-repo GitHub issue)
```

Section guidance:

| Section | Required? | When to drop it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Why | Always | Never. If you can't write a specific one, the work isn't ready. |
| Trade-offs | When meaningful alternatives existed | Obvious one-way changes, fixes to clear bugs |
| Risks | When the change has non-trivial blast radius | Docs, comments, isolated refactors with coverage |
| Test plan | When testing required judgment calls | Small changes with full unit coverage |
| Links | If any upstream artifact exists | True greenfield work with no ticket, spec, or predecessor PR |

### Step 8: Show the draft. Wait for confirmation. (Single approval gate before push.)

**This is the only user-approval gate in the workflow, and it sits immediately before `git push`.** Steps 3–5 (commit, squash, roborev) must already be complete by the time you reach it — by construction the agent cannot honor a "yes" without having walked the roborev gate first.

Show the draft title, the draft body, **and the roborev outcome** so the user can see the gate was walked. Even if the user said "create a PR", they agreed to the action, not blind-trusted your draft.

**Shortcut:** If the user re-sends this *exact* create_pr prompt verbatim, or an explicit approval phrase like "create/open the PR now," immediately after the agent has already shown a draft under this step, treat that as the Step 8 approval — proceed exactly as a "yes" would (Steps 9–13), don't re-run Steps 1–7 to produce a fresh draft. Anything else — a revision request, a question about the draft, or a paraphrase — is not the shortcut; treat it as normal feedback and re-show the draft.

Format the preview as:

```text
Title: <draft title>

Body:
---
<draft body>
---

Roborev: <clean (after M fix rounds) | N findings unresolved (list them) | unavailable (reason)>

Push and create this PR? (or edit before I submit)
```

The roborev line is mandatory — never omit it. If it shows "unavailable", the user is implicitly being asked to proceed without review.

If the user requests edits, revise and re-show. Don't auto-submit. A "yes" here authorizes closing or linking the GitHub issue (Step 9), the rebase (Step 10), the push (Step 11), and the PR creation (Step 12) — proceed through all of them without re-prompting (pausing only if the rebase hits conflicts).

### Step 9: Note the GitHub issue disposition

If Step 2 identified a GitHub issue this PR addresses, carry its disposition forward — the actual action happens in Step 12b, once a PR URL exists:

- **Same-repo issue, fully resolved by this PR** — the `Closes #NNN` line already lives in the PR body (Step 7's Links section). Nothing further is needed here: GitHub auto-closes the issue when the PR merges into `main`. Don't `gh issue close` it now — the fix isn't on `main` yet.
- **Cross-repo issue, or only partially resolved** — GitHub's closing keywords don't work across repos and shouldn't be used for partial work. Remember to leave a linking comment in Step 12b instead of closing it.
- **Ambiguous whether this PR fully resolves it** — this should already have been resolved in Step 2; if it wasn't, ask the user now rather than guessing at merge-closing behavior.
- Skip silently if no GitHub issue was identified in Step 2.
- Already authorized by the Step 8 "yes" — don't re-prompt.

### Step 10: Rebase onto the latest base (last step before opening the PR)

**This is the final step before the PR is opened.** Immediately before pushing, rebase the branch onto the freshest base so the PR opens against current `main` and merge conflicts surface here — locally, where they're cheap to resolve — instead of in GitHub's merge UI.

This must happen **before** the first push (Step 11), not after. Rebasing a branch that's already on `origin` would require a force-push, which is forbidden without explicit user approval.

```bash
git fetch origin
git rebase origin/main   # or the confirmed base branch from pre-flight
```

- If the rebase is clean, proceed to Step 11.
- If the rebase hits conflicts, **stop and surface them to the user.** Resolve them (or have the user resolve them), then re-run Steps 4–5 (re-squash if needed, re-run `roborev review --wait`) so the review reflects the rebased history. Never `git rebase --skip` or abandon conflicting hunks silently.
- If the branch is already up to date with the base, the rebase is a no-op — proceed.

### Step 11: Push the branch

Once the rebase is clean, push the branch to `origin` with upstream tracking.

```bash
git push -u origin "$(git branch --show-current)"
```

Confirm the push succeeded before moving on. If it fails (auth, protected branch, non-fast-forward), surface the error and stop — do not force-push.

### Step 12: Create the PR

**Hard gate before running `gh pr create`: for every same-repo GitHub issue Step 2 determined this PR fully resolves, mechanically verify the drafted body contains a `Closes #NNN` / `Fixes #NNN` / `Resolves #NNN` line for *that specific* issue number before shelling out — one PR can fully resolve more than one issue, and each needs its own closing reference, not just the first.** This is a real known failure mode, not a hypothetical: gtm-sdk#609 was fully fixed by gtm-sdk#628, but the drafted body only listed "gtm-sdk#609" under Links without a closing keyword, so GitHub never auto-closed it and it sat open until manually closed later. A "the plan said to add it" belief is not sufficient — grep the actual string you're about to pass to `--body` for the pattern before running the command, once per fully-resolved issue number:

```bash
grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY"
```

`\b` is not portable to the BSD `grep` on macOS — use the `([^[:alnum:]_]|$)` form above instead, which matches the same "word boundary or end of string" intent on both BSD and GNU grep.

If that grep fails for any fully-resolved issue number, **stop and fix the body** — don't proceed to `gh pr create` with a body that silently downgraded to a bare reference. If Step 2 flagged partial/cross-repo instead, the grep is expected to fail and that's correct — don't add the keyword in that case.

To make this checkable, assign the HEREDOC to `PR_BODY` first, grep that exact variable, then pass it to `--body` — don't construct the body inline in the `gh pr create` call, since there's nothing to grep before shelling out:

```bash
PR_BODY="$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why
... (real newlines, not \n)
EOF
)"

for ISSUE_NUMBER in "${FULLY_RESOLVED_ISSUE_NUMBERS[@]}"; do  # every issue Step 2 flagged as fully resolved
  grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY" || {
    echo "missing closing keyword for #${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >&2
    exit 1
  }
done

gh pr create --title "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup that double-charged credits" --body "$PR_BODY"
```

Return the PR URL to the user. Don't add follow-up commentary unless the user asks — the URL is the work product.

### Step 12b: Link the GitHub issue, if Step 9 deferred it

Only applies when Step 9 flagged a **cross-repo or partially-resolved** issue — the fully-resolved same-repo case already carries its `Closes #NNN` in the PR body and needs no action here.

```bash
gh issue comment <number> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>"                    # same-repo, partial
gh issue comment <number> --repo <owner/repo> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>" # cross-repo — use the owner/repo saved in Step 2
```

- `<PR URL>` is the output from Step 12 — this step cannot run before Step 12 for exactly that reason.
- Do not close the issue yourself; partial or cross-repo work isn't the maintainer's signal to close it.
- Skip silently if Step 9 found nothing to do here.

### Step 13: Suggest the merge once tests and checks pass

Merging is never automatic. Once the PR is open, check its status with a single call (`gh pr checks <pr-number>`). When tests and required checks have passed, suggest merging with the GitHub CLI and wait for the user to say yes:

```bash
gh pr merge <pr-number> --squash
```

- Do not poll in a loop. If checks are still running, report that and stop; the user can ask again later.
- Do not log in to, configure, or call any merge-queue service. If `gh` is not authenticated, say so and stop.
- Never pass `--admin` or `--auto` unless the user asks for it.

## Modifiers: drafts, reviewers, labels

`gh pr create` accepts modifiers that don't affect the description but matter for the PR's lifecycle. Don't auto-set any of these; only pass what the user explicitly asks for:

| Flag | When |
| --- | --- |
| `--draft` | User says "draft", or commit history shows clear in-progress markers ("WIP", "spike"). |
| `--reviewer <handle>` | Only when the user names reviewers. Don't guess. |
| `--label <name>` | Only labels that exist (`gh label list`). Invented labels silently no-op. |
| `--assignee <handle>` | Default to `@me` unless told otherwise. |
| `--base <branch>` | Only override the default branch when the user says so. |

## Anti-patterns

These show up in autogenerated PR descriptions and this skill must actively avoid them. Several come from defaults baked into other tools — including the default `gh pr create` template suggested by the Bash tool — and this skill overrides them.

### Don't summarize the diff

```markdown
## Summary
- Added `retry_with_backoff` helper in `apollo/client.py`
- Updated `enrich_account` to use it
- Added 3 unit tests in `test_apollo.py`
```

The reviewer is about to read the diff. This is duplicate work that rots the moment the diff changes. Replace with **Why**.

### Don't write empty sections

```markdown
## Risks
None.

## Test plan
Tested locally.
```

"None" and "Tested locally" carry zero signal. Drop the section.

### Don't add AI attribution

The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) prohibit AI attribution in commits and PRs.
**Never** emit:

- `Co-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>`
- `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](...)`
- Any "Generated by ..." or "Powered by ..." footer

The Bash tool's default PR template includes the 🤖 footer. **Strip it.** This skill overrides that default.

### Don't restate the title

If the title is "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup", the description shouldn't open with "This PR fixes a race in the Apollo enrichment dedup logic." Start the Why with the problem, not a rephrase.

### Don't pad with boilerplate

- "This PR makes some improvements to ..."
- "As discussed offline, ..."
- "Cleaning up some technical debt ..."

If you can't write a specific Why, pause and ask the user. Vague motivation is a tell that the work isn't ready for review.

### Don't paste test output

The Test plan section is about the *reasoning* behind what was tested. A reviewer can run the tests. They cannot rederive your reasoning from the output.

### Don't include "Closes #NNN" without confirming

GitHub auto-closes referenced issues on merge. Only use `Closes` / `Fixes` / `Resolves` keywords if Step 2 confirmed the PR fully resolves a **same-repo** issue. For partial work or a cross-repo issue, mention it in Links instead and leave a linking comment on the issue in Step 12b — no magic keyword. Skipping the confirmation in Step 2 is a bug, not a safe default: it leaves the issue open with no trace back to the PR that addressed it.

### Don't autopilot the PR submission

Even if the user said "create a PR for this", they agreed to the action, not to a specific draft. Show the draft, wait for confirmation, then submit.

## Examples

### Example 1: Small bug fix — Why + Links only

**Title:** `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts`

**Body:**

```markdown
## Why
The Apollo `search_people` paginator was dropping the last page of results because the cursor check used `>` instead of `>=`. Affected every batch where total results were an exact multiple of page_size — roughly 10% of runs. Caught when a TAM build was missing ~50 known contacts ([AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)).

## Links
- Linear: [AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)
```

(Trade-offs, Risks, Test plan dropped — small obvious fix, full coverage exists.)

### Example 2: Refactor — Why + Trade-offs + Risks + Links

**Title:** `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear → Attio sync`

**Body:**

```markdown
## Why
Five call sites in `libs/attio/` were duplicating retry/backoff logic, and each had drifted: `update_person` retried on 5xx but not 429; `create_person` retried on 429 but with no backoff; `list_workspaces` did no retry at all. The new Linear → Attio sync was about to become the sixth divergent copy.

Pulling the logic into `@retry_with_backoff` lets callers opt in with one line and ensures consistent behavior across all Attio writes.

## Trade-offs
Considered `tenacity` instead. Rejected because the call sites already have idiosyncratic logic — custom backoff that respects Attio's `Retry-After` header — that `tenacity` would require a custom wait strategy to express. The hand-rolled decorator is ~30 lines and stays close to the Attio-specific behavior.

## Risks
Changes the *shape* of exceptions that bubble up: `AttioRateLimit` is now wrapped in `RetryExhausted` after N attempts. Two existing callers caught `AttioRateLimit` directly; both updated in this PR. Grep for `AttioRateLimit` returns no other matches.

## Links
- Linear: [AI-2891](https://linear.app/...)
- Spec: design/backlog-202604010000-attio_retry_decorator-spec-01.md
```

### Example 3: Bad → Good

**Bad:**

```markdown
## Summary
- Added retry decorator
- Updated 5 Attio call sites
- Removed duplicate retry code
- Added tests

## Test plan
- [x] Ran tests
- [x] Tested locally

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```

What's wrong: the Summary paraphrases the diff, the Test plan has no reasoning, the AI footer is forbidden, and there's no motivation a reviewer can use to evaluate the change.

**Good:** see Example 2.

## Failure modes and recovery

| What happened | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Linear MCP unavailable or ticket not found | Continue without the Linear context. Note in Links: "Linear ticket: AI-NNN (MCP unavailable at draft time)" and let the user fill in. |
| Branch doesn't match a Linear pattern | Skip the Linear lookup. Rely on design artifacts and conversation. |
| No design artifact, no ticket, no clear Why from the conversation | Stop. Ask the user: "I can't establish a specific Why for this PR from the available context. Can you summarize the motivation in 1-2 sentences?" |
| `gh pr create` fails (auth, network, no remote) | Surface the error to the user. Don't retry without diagnosing. |
| User rejects the draft | Take their feedback and rewrite. Don't argue. |
| User wants to skip the confirmation step | Honor it — but require an explicit "skip confirmation" or "just create it" from them. Default is to confirm. |

## Common pitfalls

| Pitfall | Why it bites | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drafting before pre-flight checks | PR opened against stale base, with uncommitted work left behind | Run the pre-flight batch first |
| Not checking for an existing PR | Duplicate PR, or `gh pr create` errors out | Always `gh pr view` first |
| Pasting the Linear ticket verbatim | Description becomes a wall of duplicated text | Paraphrase the problem statement; link the rest |
| Filling all sections regardless of signal | Skim-defeating filler | Drop sections that don't carry meaning |
| Autopiloting `gh pr create` | Premature publication; harder to retract than to delay | Show draft, wait for confirmation |
| Inheriting the default 🤖 footer | Violates the repo's no-AI-attribution rule | Strip it from the body |
| Trusting a clean roborev as proof the code runs | Roborev reviews the diff, not test execution — a hardcoded test assertion (e.g. a literal YAML `if:` string) can still fail in CI | Run the mirrored test file / grep for affected literals before roborev (Step 5) |
| Using "WIP" in title instead of `--draft` | Title noise; doesn't actually mark the PR as draft | Use `gh pr create --draft` and a clean title |
| Linking to the PR's own branch name as "context" | The branch is implicit; this is noise | Only link to artifacts that aren't already obvious from the PR |
| Forgetting the linked GitHub issue entirely | Issue lingers open after merge with no trace back to the PR that fixed it | Resolve it in Step 2, `Closes #NNN` in Step 7, record disposition in Step 9, comment in Step 12b |
| Drafting `Closes #NNN` in Step 7 but the final body sent to `gh pr create` drops it (edits, re-drafts, template drift) | Issue never auto-closes even though Step 2/9 correctly flagged full resolution — happened for real on gtm-sdk#609/#628 | Step 12's mechanical grep gate on the literal `--body` string, not on what Step 7 intended to write |

## Red flags (stop and rethink)

- **About to `git push` without running `roborev review --wait` first.** This is the repository-wide roborev gate defined in the repo's agent instructions; no PR should skip it.
- **About to `git push` with more commits than the PR needs.** Squash to a coherent set first (Step 4); don't rely on GitHub's "Squash and merge" button to clean up history before review.
- Drafting a PR with no Linear ticket, no design artifact, and no conversation-derived motivation.
- Writing more than 3 paragraphs in Why. If you need that much, the work is probably two PRs.
- Including a `## Summary` section. This is the default template's tell — replace with `## Why`.
- Including a 🤖 footer.
- More than 5 bullets in any one section. Each bullet should be load-bearing.
- A title that ends in a period, or starts with "Update", "Fix some", "Misc", "Various".
- A title that uses a Conventional Commits prefix (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`). PR titles are formal sentences, not commit subjects.
- A title that describes *what* the diff does (e.g., "Add X helper", "Refactor Y module") when a *why* framing was available.
